newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turk lawyer says Nadir to bounce back from "plot".
newsitem.headline: Turk lawyer says Nadir to bounce back from "plot".

text.p: A lawyer for fugitive Turkish Cypriot tycoon Asil Nadir said on Wednesday his client was innocent and would bounce back stronger than ever from the "plot" against him, Anatolian news agency reported.

"Asil Nadir is innocent. He has returned to his country and will be born again stronger than before," lawyer Ali Riza Gorgun told reporters waiting outside the hotel where Nadir is staying on a business trip to Istanbul.
Nadir jumped bail in Britain in May 1993 while awaiting trial on theft and false accounting charges related to the collapse of his Polly Peck fruit-to-electronics empire.
Nadir, who also holds a Turkish passport, flew to Turkey on his first trip out of his native north Cyprus since he fled there from British justice four years ago.
Turkish police said on Tuesday they would not hand Nadir over to British authorities, but Gorgun suggested there was a possibility he would return to Britain voluntarily.
Speaking at his hotel near the Bosphorus Strait, Nadir said he had come to complete business "left half finished in the past". Aides did not say what business he was referring to.
When asked Nadir's reaction to Britain's request to have him extradited, Gorgun said: "He looked out to the Bosphorus and said 'those British are unbelievable people'".
Britain and NATO ally Turkey do not have an extradition treaty but usually hand over criminal suspects to each other under a Council of Europe agreement.
The British embassy in Ankara said earlier it hoped Turkish police would arrest the fallen magnate on the strength of an Interpol "wanted" notice.
The London Times said earlier this month that policemen acting for the Serious Fraud Office had been sent to Turkey to seek Nadir's arrest after the businessman said he would fly to Istanbul.
